a global calibration is never as accurate as a local one, but that augmenting a global calibration with local samples often improves predictions relative to the global calibration alone.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
a large, diverse global library is a valuable resource, but that it can be augmented with relatively few local soil samples to improve predictions of clay, SOC, or IC for a given site.
the best VisNIR-DSR predictions of soil clay, soil organic C, and inorganic C can be made with a local+global calibration using a large global library and a small local library.
the more local calibration data that are available, the more valuable they are for improving the prediction of soil properties using VisNIR-DSR.
The main takeaway from our work is that
augmenting a global VisNIR spectral library with a few local samples can substantially improve predictions of soil properties.
local+global VisNIR-DSR calibrations can be a useful compromise between the accuracy of local calibrations and the cost of acquiring local calibration samples.

the use of local+global calibrate VisNIR-DSR models is an effective strategy for improving the accuracy of VisNIR-DrS predictions in regions where the soil spectral library is not sufficiently representative of the soil types in the area of interest.
